Synopsis:
Crime reaction for Chop, the Colony Butcher, after we either free Us from its cage, mess with the cage or kill Us.

Cluster Contexts:
- COL_Morgue_Butcher_FreedUs.json: This exchange happens amid the chaotic aftermath of the goblin assault on the Druid Grove: defenders and refugees are exhausted and leaders and druids are sorting out prisoners and damage. A caged creature called "Us" is on scene and Chop — the Colony Butcher, an enforcer figure tied to the goblin side — catches the player messing with its cage and objects loudly. Chop treats touching, removing, or killing the captive as a serious offense (theft, desecration, or murder), so the player's lines ("we are alike," "let me take it") are offered as justifications or challenges to that claim. Off‑screen people who matter here include druids, tiefling refugees, and other captives (e.g., the goblin Sazza), and prior choices in the assault shape how angry or conciliatory Chop will be.
- COL_Morgue_Us.json: Default dialogue with Us while they are in the Colony. Us is either locked in a cage in the Morgue, trying to sneak away from the Butcher, or thanking you for saving them, after which they will disappear.
- NGB_Warning_Vandalise.json: A player damaged or destroyedf an item owned by an NPC, and an NPC (the owner or someone else) witnessed this and stops the player by starting this dialog.
-- Can check the GEB_Crime_IsVictim flag on speaker 1 to distinguish the NPC from being the victim (= owner) or a witness of the crime.
- NGB_Warning_Theft.json: A player stole something, an NPC witness this act, and starts this dialog with the player
-- Can check the GEB_Crime_IsVictim flag on speaker 1 to distinguish the NPC from being the victim or a witness of the crime.
- LOW_NGB_SharGrotto_Trespassing.json: Trespass NGB dialogue with a Shar Grotto guard. Narrator lines indicate how the player has been caught where they shouldn't be.

context: After a chaotic goblin assault on the Druid Grove, defenders and refugees are exhausted and leaders/druids are sorting prisoners and damage in the morgue; a caged creature called "Us" is on scene. Chop is the Colony Butcher — an enforcer tied to the goblin side — and he treats anyone touching, removing, or killing the captive as committing a serious offense (theft, desecration, or murder). This exchange is triggered when Chop catches the player meddling with Us' cage; the player's lines are offered as justifications, challenges, or attempts to take Us. Off‑screen people who matter include druids, tiefling refugees, and other captives (e.g., the goblin Sazza), and earlier choices during the assault influence how angry or conciliatory Chop will be.
